scenes.visual: Full-frame cross-section of one dark-slate cell (plasma membrane across top, cytoplasm filling the middle, rounded nucleus at bottom) occupying 70% of frame height. On the right sits a live schematic level tank with a steady tap pouring bright coral-orange β-catenin particles in and an open violet drain sweeping them out. High-contrast title fades cleanly over the upper membrane: 'Wnt Slows the Drain'.

scenes.tts: Why would a cell make a protein all day, only to destroy it? Most of your cells do exactly that with free beta-catenin. It looks like waste, yet it is a fast, responsive control switch.
scenes.caption: Why would a cell make a protein all day, only to destroy it? Most of your cells do exactly that with free β-catenin. It looks like waste, yet it is a fast, responsive control switch.
scenes.visual: Carried cell cross-section stays full frame. Bright coral-orange β-catenin blocks continuously emerge from a synthesis tap on the left of the cytoplasm, drift rightward, and vanish into a violet shredder on the right, keeping the right-side schematic level bar low and steady.
scenes.narration: Why would a cell make a protein all day, only to destroy it? Most of your cells do exactly that with free β-catenin. It looks like waste, yet it is a fast, responsive control switch.

scenes.tts: Start with a cell receiving no signal. Stable beta-catenin sits locked at cell junctions, untouched here. Every free copy meets the destruction complex. A violet scaffold called Axin holds two kinases beside beta-catenin. A large partner called APC helps the complex finish its job.
scenes.caption: Start with a cell receiving no signal. Stable β-catenin sits locked at cell junctions, untouched here. Every free copy meets the destruction complex. A violet scaffold called Axin holds two kinases beside β-catenin. A large partner called APC helps the complex finish its job.
scenes.visual: Left cell border briefly highlights locked coral β-catenin blocks anchored at a cadherin junction (label: 'Junction pool: stable', then dimmed aside). Centre cytoplasm highlights the violet destruction-complex ring carrying four labelled blocks: 'Axin', 'APC', 'CK1', 'GSK3'. A free coral β-catenin block docks inside the ring while teal 'Frizzled' and slate-blue 'LRP5/6' sit empty on the top membrane.
scenes.narration: Start with a cell receiving no signal. Stable β-catenin sits locked at cell junctions, untouched here. Every free copy meets the destruction complex. A violet scaffold called Axin holds two kinases beside β-catenin. A large partner called APC helps the complex finish its job.

scenes.tts: First, CK one adds a priming phosphate to beta-catenin. That lets GSK three add three more phosphates in sequence. Next, beta T R C P grips the tagged protein inside an SCF ubiquitin ligase. The proteasome then shreds it.
scenes.caption: First, CK1 adds a priming phosphate to β-catenin. That lets GSK3 add three more phosphates in sequence. Next, β-TrCP grips the tagged protein inside an SCF ubiquitin ligase. The proteasome then shreds it.
scenes.visual: Inside the violet destruction complex, 'CK1' stamps one glowing gold phosphate dot onto coral β-catenin, then 'GSK3' stamps three more dots in order ('schematic'). The tagged β-catenin slides to a violet 'SCF (β-TrCP)' clamp, grows a chain of small ubiquitin beads, and spirals into a turning proteasome cylinder, leaving faint drifting fragments. In the nucleus below, emerald 'TCF' sits on DNA holding cool grey-blue 'Groucho' ('Target genes: OFF').
scenes.narration: First, CK1 adds a priming phosphate to β-catenin. That lets GSK3 add three more phosphates in sequence. Next, β-TrCP grips the tagged protein inside an SCF ubiquitin ligase. The proteasome then shreds it.

scenes.tts: Now picture the steady level of free beta-catenin like water in a tank. A running tap sets synthesis, while an open drain sets destruction. If a signal slows destruction to one quarter while synthesis stays steady, how does the level change?
scenes.caption: Now picture the steady level of free β-catenin like water in a tank. A running tap sets synthesis, while an open drain sets destruction. If a signal slows destruction to one quarter while synthesis stays steady, how does the level change?
scenes.visual: The right-hand schematic level tank expands smoothly beside the cell. A steady inflow stream ('Synthesis: 12 / min') pours coral fluid in while an open outflow pipe ('Destruction k: 0.4 / min') holds the fluid flat at '30 units' ('schematic'). A valve narrows the drain to 'k: 0.1 / min (1/4 rate)'. Top question banner reads 'Destruction cut to 1/4, synthesis steady: steady level?' above three clean choice pills: 'Stays flat', 'Drops to 1/4', and 'Rises 4x'.
scenes.narration: Now picture the steady level of free β-catenin like water in a tank. A running tap sets synthesis, while an open drain sets destruction. If a signal slows destruction to one quarter while synthesis stays steady, how does the level change?

scenes.visual: Hold the narrowed-drain tank and the three choice pills on screen for 4.5 seconds while gentle coral ripples shimmer at the water line and a quiet radial countdown ring completes one smooth turn.

scenes.tts: The level rises fourfold. At steady state, level equals synthesis divided by the destruction rate. Twelve over point four gives thirty, but twelve over point one gives one hundred twenty. Synthesis never changed. That is how the signal we meet next, Wint, raises free beta-catenin: by slowing its constant destruction.
scenes.caption: The level rises fourfold. At steady state, level equals synthesis divided by the destruction rate. 12 over 0.4 gives 30, but 12 over 0.1 gives 120. Synthesis never changed. That is how the signal we meet next, Wnt, raises free β-catenin: by slowing its constant destruction.
scenes.visual: Choice pill 'Rises 4x' highlights in emerald as the other two fade. Coral fluid in the schematic tank rises along a computed exponential approach curve to '120 units (4x higher)' with the formula 'Level = synthesis ÷ destruction' ('12 ÷ 0.1 = 120'). The tank then shrinks smoothly back to the right-side gauge as focus moves up to the plasma membrane. Empathy fix: Show 'Level = synthesis ÷ destruction rate' as the rule is spoken, then both cases in turn as spoken: '12 ÷ 0.4 = 30', then '12 ÷ 0.1 = 120 (4x)'.
scenes.narration: The level rises fourfold. At steady state, level equals synthesis divided by the destruction rate. 12 over 0.4 gives 30, but 12 over 0.1 gives 120. Synthesis never changed. That is how the signal we meet next, Wnt, raises free β-catenin: by slowing its constant destruction.

scenes.tts: That signal is Wint, a secreted protein carrying a fatty acid tail. Outside the cell, Wint grips a teal receptor called Frizzled using that lipid tail. At the same time, Wint brings Frizzled together with a slate-blue partner, LRP five or six.
scenes.caption: That signal is Wnt, a secreted protein carrying a fatty acid tail. Outside the cell, Wnt grips a teal receptor called Frizzled using that lipid tail. At the same time, Wnt brings Frizzled together with a slate-blue partner, LRP5 or LRP6.
scenes.visual: A gold 'Wnt' block carrying a curved gold lipid tail drifts down to the top membrane. Its lipid tail tucks into a groove on teal seven-pass 'Frizzled', while gold 'Wnt' bridges across to pull slate-blue single-pass 'LRP5/6' snug beside 'Frizzled'.
scenes.narration: That signal is Wnt, a secreted protein carrying a fatty acid tail. Outside the cell, Wnt grips a teal receptor called Frizzled using that lipid tail. At the same time, Wnt brings Frizzled together with a slate-blue partner, LRP5 or LRP6.

scenes.tts: Inside the cell, Frizzled recruits an amber protein called Dishevelled. Meanwhile, the inner tail of LRP six gains phosphates and grabs the Axin scaffold. The destruction complex moves up to the receptor, where it stops delivering beta-catenin efficiently to the ligase.
scenes.caption: Inside the cell, Frizzled recruits an amber protein called Dishevelled. Meanwhile, the inner tail of LRP6 gains phosphates and grabs the Axin scaffold. The destruction complex moves up to the receptor, where it stops delivering β-catenin efficiently to the ligase.
scenes.visual: An amber 'Dishevelled' block docks directly beneath teal 'Frizzled'. Gold phosphate dots appear along the intracellular tail of slate-blue 'LRP5/6'. The violet destruction complex ('Axin', 'APC', 'CK1', 'GSK3') glides upward from the cytoplasm and tethers to the phosphorylated 'LRP5/6' tail; a clean note beside it reads 'How complex stops: debated'. The violet shredder below idles slowly.
scenes.narration: Inside the cell, Frizzled recruits an amber protein called Dishevelled. Meanwhile, the inner tail of LRP6 gains phosphates and grabs the Axin scaffold. The destruction complex moves up to the receptor, where it stops delivering β-catenin efficiently to the ligase.

scenes.tts: How the receptor disables the complex is still debated, yet the result is clear. Newly made coral beta-catenin survives, fills the cytoplasm, and enters the nucleus. There it finds emerald TCF on target DNA, where grey Groucho kept genes off.
scenes.caption: How the receptor disables the complex is still debated, yet the result is clear. Newly made coral β-catenin survives, fills the cytoplasm, and enters the nucleus. There it finds emerald TCF on target DNA, where grey Groucho kept genes off.
scenes.visual: Free coral β-catenin blocks emerge steadily from the synthesis tap, fill the cytoplasm as the right-side schematic gauge climbs, and stream downward through nuclear pores toward emerald 'TCF' bound to DNA with cool grey-blue 'Groucho'.
scenes.narration: How the receptor disables the complex is still debated, yet the result is clear. Newly made coral β-catenin survives, fills the cytoplasm, and enters the nucleus. There it finds emerald TCF on target DNA, where grey Groucho kept genes off.

scenes.tts: In the simple model, beta-catenin displaces Groucho and brings in proteins that switch target genes on. Notice what happens if a mutation breaks APC or the phosphate sites on beta-catenin. Destruction slows even with no Wint, leaving those target genes stuck on.
scenes.caption: In the simple model, β-catenin displaces Groucho and brings in proteins that switch target genes on. Notice what happens if a mutation breaks APC or the phosphate sites on β-catenin. Destruction slows even with no Wnt, leaving those target genes stuck on.
scenes.visual: Inside the nucleus, coral β-catenin docks onto emerald 'TCF', cool grey-blue 'Groucho' drifts away (label: 'Simple model'), and bright emerald transcription waves sweep along the DNA ('Target genes: ON'). On the right, a brief schematic inset shows empty top receptors ('No Wnt') above a cracked violet 'APC' block while the coral gauge stays high and nuclear genes stay lit emerald ('Broken drain: stuck ON').
scenes.narration: In the simple model, β-catenin displaces Groucho and brings in proteins that switch target genes on. Notice what happens if a mutation breaks APC or the phosphate sites on β-catenin. Destruction slows even with no Wnt, leaving those target genes stuck on.

scenes.tts: Control over free beta-catenin rests on destruction, not synthesis. Keep the drain open and target genes stay silent. Slow the drain with Wint, and free beta-catenin climbs to switch genes on. The cell turns the pathway on by slowing constant destruction.
scenes.caption: Control over free β-catenin rests on destruction, not synthesis. Keep the drain open and target genes stay silent. Slow the drain with Wnt, and free β-catenin climbs to switch genes on. The cell turns the pathway on by slowing constant destruction.
scenes.visual: Full-frame cell glides smoothly into a clean side-by-side schematic comparison: left half 'No Wnt' (open drain, low coral β-catenin, genes OFF); right half '+ Wnt' (complex tethered at teal Frizzled and slate-blue LRP5/6 with amber Dishevelled, slowed drain, high coral β-catenin, genes ON).
scenes.narration: Control over free β-catenin rests on destruction, not synthesis. Keep the drain open and target genes stay silent. Slow the drain with Wnt, and free β-catenin climbs to switch genes on. The cell turns the pathway on by slowing constant destruction.
